questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: Which is outside the opening tubal-cause trio in Female Infertility Part 2?
questions.exp: PID, salpingitis and endometriosis are bracketed as causes of unilateral or bilateral tubal blockage.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: The initial investigation of choice for tubal patency in this chapter is ____.
questions.exp: HSG is labelled IOC; laparoscopic chromopertubation is separately labelled the gold standard.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: HSG introduces ____ into the uterus and follows it using ____.
questions.exp: HSG assesses contrast passage and spillage on serial radiographs.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: HSG shows contrast spilling freely on both sides. Which interpretation fits the image caption?
questions.exp: The illustrated HSG is captioned bilateral spilling of dye.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: The cannula pictured beside the HSG section is the ____ cannula.
questions.exp: The spiral-tipped illustration is labelled Leech Wilkinson; Rubin appears later with CO2 insufflation.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: The source schedules HSG on cycle days ____.
questions.exp: Days 7–10 are in the early postmenstrual, preovulatory interval used in this work-up.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: An HSG is painful and reports cornual blockage, but a later test finds patency. Which limitation explains the discrepancy?
opts: Cornual spasm causing a false-positive block
Contrast guarantees elimination of all spasms
questions.exp: The chapter explicitly links pain to cornual spasm and false-positive tubal blockage.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: I) HSG visualises the exterior of the tubes. II) Pain during HSG can cause cornual spasm.
questions.exp: HSG does not visualise the tubal exterior; pain-induced spasm can mimic obstruction.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: Match basic investigations: 1) Female 2) Male 3) Female >35 years, additional with A) Sperm analysis B) HSG and ovulation tests C) Reserve tests.
questions.exp: The side note assigns HSG/ovulation to females, semen to males and reserve testing to older females.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: The gold-standard tubal-patency test is ____.
questions.exp: It allows direct observation of dye spillage and the tubal exterior.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: The two dyes named for laparoscopic chromopertubation are ____.
questions.exp: The blue dyes are used for direct laparoscopic visualisation; HSG requires radiopaque contrast.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: Order the laparoscopic test: A) Observe spillage B) Insert laparoscope C) Pass dye through the cannula.
questions.exp: The procedural list runs insertion, dye passage, then direct visualisation.

questions.sec: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.unit: Tubal causes, HSG and chromopertubation
questions.q: Peritubal adhesions need assessment as well as patency. Which advantage favours laparoscopy over HSG?
opts: Direct visualisation of the tubal exterior
No need for any uterine dye passage
questions.exp: The stated advantage is visualising the exterior, which HSG cannot show.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: One tube is blocked and the other is patent. What pathway does the source assign to unilateral tubal block?
opts: Manage like unexplained infertility: clomiphene plus IUI
Immediate donor-oocyte IVF in every case
questions.exp: The unilateral branch is explicitly managed like unexplained infertility, unlike confirmed bilateral disease.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: HSG suggests bilateral block. What is the confirmation step in the main algorithm?
questions.exp: The bilateral branch proceeds to laparoscopy before differentiating proximal and distal block.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: Bilateral proximal block is also called ____ block; bilateral distal block is ____ block.
questions.exp: The algorithm uses proximal/cornual and distal/fimbrial as paired terms.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: The commonest cause of apparent bilateral proximal/cornual block in the notes is ____.
questions.exp: Spasm is the commonest overall cause; TB is specifically the commonest pathological cause in this source.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: Proximal obstruction may be due to cornual spasm or a mucus plug. Which procedure is the next directed step?
questions.exp: A guide wire is passed from the uterus into the tube under hysteroscopic guidance.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: Hysteroscopic tubal cannulation aims both to ____ and to ____.
opts: Release cornual spasm; dislodge mucus plugs
questions.exp: These two actions are explicitly listed under cannulation.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: After the cannulation branch, the next assessment named is ____.
questions.exp: The source returns to laparoscopic confirmation of tubal passage.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: The commonest pathological cause of bilateral cornual block in these notes is ____, with fertility management listed as ____.
questions.exp: The TB branch distinguishes pathological obstruction from physiological spasm; active TB still requires appropriate treatment.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: Laparoscopy confirms bilateral fimbrial block. Besides confirming diagnosis, what determines the next treatment branch?
questions.exp: Mild disease and severe disease/hydrosalpinx have different paths in the diagram.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: Mild fimbrial disease is treated in the diagram by ____, using small nicks at the fimbrial ends.
questions.exp: Fimbrioplasty aims to reopen the distal fimbrial end in mild disease.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: Severe bilateral fimbrial disease has produced hydrosalpinx. Which fertility route is shown?
questions.exp: The severe-disease branch leads to IVF; hydrosalpinx is addressed before transfer.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: The management of choice in tubal infertility is stated as ____.
questions.exp: This explicit note follows the mild/severe distal-disease branches.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: Hydrosalpinx is a collection of ____ within the fallopian tube; the fluid is labelled ____.
questions.exp: The source distinguishes retained tubal secretions from blood or pus and notes their adverse reproductive effect.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: Before IVF, a hydrosalpinx risks exposing the uterus to harmful fluid. Which two preparatory alternatives are listed?
opts: Fimbrioplasty or IUI without fluid isolation
Cervical dilatation or luteal progesterone only
questions.exp: Either proximal isolation or tube removal is followed by IVF in the diagram.

questions.sec: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.unit: Unilateral, cornual and fimbrial block algorithms
questions.q: Match 1) Mild distal disease 2) Severe hydrosalpinx before IVF 3) Suspected cornual spasm with A) Cannulation B) Fimbrioplasty C) Clip/salpingectomy.
questions.exp: Location and severity, rather than a single universal operation, determine these source pathways.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: A mid-segment tubal block occurs at the ____ and is the typical site of ____.
questions.exp: The continuation above uterine causes describes an isthmic block after permanent tubal ligation.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: Recanalisation after tubal ligation is described as being undertaken in ____ circumstances.
questions.exp: Sterilisation is intended as permanent; reversal is an exceptional rather than guaranteed pathway.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: Which patient factor favours successful tubal reversal in the source list?
opts: Undetectable ovarian reserve at any age
Menopause for more than five years
questions.exp: Age under 35 is the first favourable factor.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: The preferred reversal anastomosis is ____ over ____.
questions.exp: The source ranks like-calibre isthmo-isthmic anastomosis above isthmo-ampullary.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: A favourable reconstructed tubal length is ____.
questions.exp: The source's threshold is >4 cm after reconstruction.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: Which prior sterilisation method is more favourable for reversal in the notes?
opts: Fimbriectomy over either clips or rings
questions.exp: The list gives Hulka clips > Fallope rings, reflecting less tubal destruction.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: I) The notes say the ligation-to-reversal interval determines tubal reversal success. II) They contrast this with vasectomy reversal.
questions.exp: The note says tubal reversal chances do not depend on interval, unlike vasectomy; this is the source's comparison.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: A cavity-distorting fibroid is linked to infertility. Which type and fertility-preserving operation are paired?
questions.exp: The uterine-cause list names submucous fibroid most commonly and myomectomy as management.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: Which is a cervical rather than uterine factor in the page's lists?
questions.exp: The uterine block includes polyps, adhesions and chronic endometritis; antibodies appear under cervical causes.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: Chronic endometritis in the uterine-cause list is attributed to ____.
questions.exp: The source specifically writes chronic endometritis due to chlamydia.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: A woman exposed to DES in utero has a uterine factor. Which shape is associated with that exposure?
questions.exp: DES exposure is linked to a T-shaped or hypoplastic uterus.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: Mullerian malformations more commonly cause ____ than infertility, although ____ may cause infertility.
questions.exp: The note distinguishes reproductive loss from failure to conceive and singles out septate uterus.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: Match 1) Uterine cavity investigation labelled gold standard 2) Initial imaging listed with it with A) USG B) Hysteroscopy.
questions.exp: USG and hysteroscopy are listed together; hysteroscopy is explicitly labelled gold standard in this uterine-cavity context.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: A Mullerian malformation may be a ____ finding during the uterine work-up.
questions.exp: The bracket beside USG and hysteroscopy notes coincidental identification of a malformation.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: Which does NOT belong to the cervical-cause trio?
questions.exp: Chronic endometritis belongs to the uterine list; the other three are cervical factors.

questions.sec: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.unit: Mid-segment reversal, uterine and cervical factors
questions.q: Antisperm antibodies in females are described as ____ and as an ____ cause of infertility.
questions.exp: The final lines identify both the sperm-killing effect and the immunological category.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: The obsolete postcoital test for antisperm antibodies is also called the ____ test.
questions.exp: Huhner is the historical postcoital test; Rubin concerns CO2 tubal insufflation.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: The Huhner-test timing is days ____ with a cervical smear within ____ after intercourse.
questions.exp: Both cycle day and postcoital collection interval are specified in the historical protocol.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: Match sperm motion in the Huhner diagram: 1) Progressive 2) Rotatory with A) Antisperm antibodies B) Normal.
questions.exp: Forward progressive movement is normal; rotatory motion suggests antibodies in this obsolete test.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: Why do the notes group cervical causes with unexplained infertility rather than routinely perform ASA testing?
opts: Huhner testing is the best current reserve test
Both are treated with clomiphene plus IUI in the stated pathway
IUI requires complete bilateral tubal block
questions.exp: The management is the same in the notes, so the obsolete ASA test does not alter the pathway.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: Clomiphene may start on any day from ____ and continues for ____.
questions.exp: The source gives a start window of D2–D5 and a five-day course.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: The common clomiphene course highlighted is days ____.
questions.exp: D5–D9 is the most commonly written five-day schedule in this block.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: After clomiphene, monitoring starts on day 10. A follicle reaches ≥17 mm. Which trigger is named?
questions.exp: hCG triggers ovulation; the source notes that a trigger is not absolutely necessary in every cycle.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: After the hCG trigger, IUI is timed approximately ____ later in this protocol.
questions.exp: The arrow between trigger and IUI is labelled 32–36 hours.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: I) hCG triggering is described as absolutely compulsory in every clomiphene-IUI cycle. II) Follicular monitoring begins on day 10 in this example.
questions.exp: The source says the trigger is not absolutely necessary, while monitoring begins D10.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: HyCoSy stands for ____.
questions.exp: The term refers to ultrasound assessment of contrast passage through the tubes.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: The source's Lignosol mixture for HyCoSy contains ____.
questions.exp: The contrast-enhancing mixture is injected into the uterus and followed through the tubes by ultrasound.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: A patient wants a less painful outpatient tubal-patency assessment without serial X-rays. Which named method fits the listed advantages?
questions.exp: HyCoSy is described as OPD, less painful, safe and cost-effective; tubal passage is visualised sonographically.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: Which is NOT a stated advantage of HyCoSy?
opts: Direct laparoscopic inspection of peritubal adhesions
questions.exp: Direct external inspection is the advantage of laparoscopy, not HyCoSy.

questions.sec: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.unit: Postcoital test, stimulation-IUI and alternative tubal tests
questions.q: Rubin's cannula belongs to the obsolete ____ test for ____.
questions.exp: The illustration and caption identify Rubin's CO2 insufflation test as an obsolete patency test.
